name: Adjacent Square Completions Preserve Dismantlability
statement: Let nonempty ample $G\subseteq Q_F$ have two absent adjacent concepts $c,u$ such that each individual addition is ample and acquires the same two-coordinate support. Then $H=G\cup\{c,u\}$ is ample, and $H$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $G$ is dismantlable ample.
proof: The two punctured squares and one added tip form a punctured three-cube at the other tip, so the one-concept extension criterion makes the double addition ample. If $G$ peels, delete the two tips and continue in $G$. Conversely take a smallest counterexample and inspect the first deletion of a peeling of $H$. A deletion outside the local three-cube yields a smaller counterexample; a neighbouring local deletion factors the residual through two rank-two additions, which preserve peelability; opposite-face deletions either commute with the second deletion or leave a family isomorphic to $G$. The added tips themselves leave a nonpeelable rank-two completion. Every case contradicts minimality or the assumed peeling of $H$.
comments: The archived verifier exercises every reduction case on three nonminimal ample controls containing the certified 291-concept cornerless family as a proper restriction.
